facts.text: Presque Isle Peninsula, the namesake of the county, hosts two historic lighthouses that once guided ships into the only natural harbor between Detroit and Mackinac.
The community of Presque Isle sits a few miles south of the peninsula and once housed the Fireside Inn, Birch Hill Hotel, and Grand Lake Hotel for vacationers.
The New Presque Isle Lighthouse, built in 1870, remains the tallest climbable tower on the Great Lakes and houses a preserved Third Order Fresnel Lens.
Presque Isle Harbor Marina, a restaurant, and a gift shop line the sandy beaches where sunrise and sunset over Lake Huron are visible from the tombolo strip.
The Presque Isle Township Museum Society celebrates maritime heritage by hosting an annual photo contest featuring the two lighthouses and surrounding range lights.
Grand Lake and Long Lake, each over 5,000 acres, are nearly identical inland lakes that have appeared twice on the Outdoor Channel’s Major League Fishing for their bass.
